clusters.label: Introduction to Word Embeddings
clusters.rationale: Both candidates introduce the concept of word embeddings as numerical representations of text for machine learning. They cover the same foundational idea.

clusters.label: One-hot Encoding
clusters.rationale: This candidate specifically covers one-hot encoding, which is a distinct simple encoding method.

clusters.label: Count-based Text Representations
clusters.rationale: These candidates cover Bag-of-Words, N-gram, and TF-IDF, and the preprocessing steps (stemming, stop-word removal) that are common to count-based methods. They describe similar foundational techniques.

clusters.label: Limitations of Count-based Methods
clusters.rationale: Both candidates explicitly list shortcomings of count-based methods, such as sparsity, lack of context, and unknown words.

clusters.label: Word Similarity and Embedding Space
clusters.rationale: These candidates explain distributional similarity (words with shared contexts are similar) and how embedding space places words so distance indicates similarity. They form a cohesive unit on semantic similarity.

clusters.label: Ideal Embedding Properties
clusters.rationale: This candidate describes what an ideal embedding space looks like: clusters of similar words and analogical relations.

clusters.label: Custom Embedding Layer Training
clusters.rationale: This candidate covers the method of training a custom embedding layer as part of a neural network model.

clusters.label: Word2vec Architectures
clusters.rationale: This candidate describes Word2vec including CBOW and Skip-gram architectures.

clusters.label: GloVe: Global Vectors
clusters.rationale: This candidate covers GloVe and its use of co-occurrence matrices to combine local and global context.

clusters.label: fastText and Subword Information
clusters.rationale: This candidate explains fastText's subword n-gram approach for handling rare and unknown words.

clusters.label: ELMo: Contextualized Word Representations
clusters.rationale: This candidate describes ELMo's dynamic, context-dependent word representations using bidirectional LSTMs.

clusters.label: Using Pre-trained Embeddings
clusters.rationale: These candidates discuss how pre-trained embeddings can be used statically or fine-tuned, and specifically the Gensim library as a tool for working with pre-trained embeddings.

clusters.label: TF-IDF Definition and Computation
clusters.rationale: These candidates define TF-IDF, explain its components (TF, IDF), and demonstrate the product computation. They form the core mathematical explanation of TF-IDF.

clusters.label: TF-IDF Applications and Document Representation
clusters.rationale: These candidates cover how TF-IDF produces document feature vectors used in classification, clustering, retrieval, and document search. They emphasize the practical outcomes and uses.

clusters.label: IDF Zero and Discriminative Power
clusters.rationale: These candidates focus on the special case when IDF is zero (term appears in all documents) and what it implies about discriminative power.

clusters.label: TF-IDF Implementation with Scikit-learn
clusters.rationale: These candidates are about practical implementation in Python: using TfidfVectorizer, stopword removal with NLTK, and preparing documents by splitting text.

clusters.label: Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) and NLP Vocabulary
clusters.rationale: These candidates introduce basic NLP terms (document, body, dictionary, topic) and define LSA as an unsupervised technique for discovering latent topics and reducing dimensionality.

clusters.label: Document-Term Matrix and SVD in LSA
clusters.rationale: These candidates explain the document-term matrix representation and the use of Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to perform dimensionality reduction in LSA.

clusters.label: Twitter Entity Sentiment Analysis Dataset
clusters.rationale: These candidates are all about the same dataset: entity-level sentiment analysis, sentiment classes, dataset split, license, and description. They form a single cluster about the dataset.
